title_original: Thelma Golden to leave Studio Museum
excerpt_original: She has been at the New York institution for over two decades

blocks.text: The long-standing head of the Studio Museum, Thelma Golden , has said she will leave the New York institution.

Her departure comes after 21 years at the helm, and one year on from opening the museum’s new David Adjaye-designed building in Harlem. While that involved the fundraising of over $300 million, it was Golden’s promotion of Black artists that forged her reputation, with the likes of Mark Bradford , Simone Leigh , Lorna Simpson and Amy Sherald receiving early support from the museum director.

Golden says she will stay on until a successor is found, with the New York Times tipping several of her former employees, including Naomi Beckwith , Rujeko Hockley, Naima J. Keith and Christine Y. Kim, as possible runners and riders. Franklin Sirmans, director of the Pérez Art Museum Miami; Sandra Jackson-Dumont, the former director and chief executive of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles; and Valerie Cassel Oliver, the curator of Modern and contemporary art at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts are also mentioned by the paper as contenders.

With Kim, Golden curated the much-quoted 2001 exhibition Freestyle , a survey of emerging Black artists. Other exhibitions have included Black Romantic: The Figurative Impulse in Contemporary African-American Art (2002), Chris Ofili: Afro Muses 1995–2005 (2005).

Kathryn C. Chenault, the museum’s chair, said, ‘For more than twenty years, Thelma Golden has defined the vision and identity of the Studio Museum in Harlem. She has elevated and strengthened this institution in every way, helped move Black artists into the center of the cultural landscape, and mentored countless Black museum professionals across the country. She is now passing on the leadership of the museum she helped build, entrusting it to a new generation she helped foster.’
